system.name: Anduril
system.one_liner: a feedback-driven fault injection tool that quickly reproduces a given fault-induced production failure in distributed systems

components.name: System code
components.role: input system bytecode analyzed and instrumented by the Instrumenter

components.name: Instrumenter
components.role: performs static causal analysis on system code and inserts fault-injection and logging code, producing a causal graph and an instrumented system

components.name: static causal graph
components.role: graph of program points (fault candidates f1-f3 linked to observation points o1-o3) potentially related to the failure symptom

components.name: Instrumented system
components.role: system code with injected fault-triggering and logging snippets, produced by the Instrumenter and run by the Explorer

components.name: Failure log (from production)
components.role: failure log collected from the uninstrumented production system, used to compute initial fault-candidate priorities

components.name: Failure oracle
components.role: checks whether a run reproduces the target failure

components.name: Workload
components.role: input workload run against the instrumented system to exercise fault candidates

components.name: Explorer
components.role: searches for the root-cause fault's location and injection timing using a feedback-driven loop over the causal graph, logs, oracle, and workload

components.name: Update priorities
components.role: recomputes fault-candidate priorities based on the causal graph and log data

components.name: Fault location and time
components.role: the highest-priority candidate fault location and injection timing chosen for the next run

components.name: Symptoms
components.role: observed behavior after running the workload with the chosen fault injected

components.name: Repro run logs (from instrumented system)
components.role: logs from an unsuccessful reproduction attempt, fed back to update priorities

components.name: script
components.role: the output reproduction script once the oracle confirms the failure is reproduced

content.key_idea: Anduril's Instrumenter statically analyzes and instruments system code into a causal graph and an instrumented system, which Explorer then searches over in an iterative feedback loop until the oracle confirms the failure is reproduced.
content.reading_order: Left to right: System code and inputs flow into Instrumenter, whose outputs feed Explorer, which cycles through the shaded feedback loop until Symptoms yields a reproduced script.

encoding.color_means: yellow fill = Anduril's two major novel components (Instrumenter, Explorer); blue causal-graph outlines mark the static-analysis output; bright-blue arrows trace the iterative feedback loop separately from the thicker gray/black one-shot data arrows
encoding.line_style_means: thick gray/black arrows carry one-shot inputs/outputs (code, logs, oracle, workload, final script); thin bright-blue arrows form the cyclic feedback loop inside the shaded 'feedback loop' region
encoding.emphasis: a shaded gray background box explicitly bounds and labels the 'feedback loop', visually separating Anduril's one-shot preprocessing (Instrumenter side) from its iterative search (Explorer's loop)
reusable_patterns: linear preprocessing pipeline feeding a hub component that then runs an explicitly boxed cyclic feedback loop
color-coded arrows distinguishing one-shot pipeline data from iterative loop signals
small labeled icons (braces, documents) standing in for code/log artifacts instead of plain boxes
weaknesses: the Failure oracle arrow terminates at the Explorer box even though the text implies the oracle is invoked specifically during the Symptoms-checking step, so its exact use within the loop is not pinpointed visually

evidence: Anduril contains two major components, Instrumenter and Explorer (Figure 2).
It performs static analysis and computes a causal graph consisting of program points potentially related to the failure symptom.
Explorer's goal is to quickly search for the location of the root-cause fault as well as the timing for injection.

summary: Anduril is a feedback-driven fault injection tool that quickly reproduces a given fault-induced production failure in distributed systems by searching for the right fault and timing. Figure 2 shows its architecture and workflow: System code feeds an Instrumenter, which performs static causal analysis to produce a static causal graph (fault candidates f1-f3 linked to observation points o1-o3) and an Instrumented system with injected fault/logging code. These, plus a production Failure log, a Failure oracle, and a Workload, feed the Explorer, which runs inside a shaded 'feedback loop': it updates fault-candidate priorities, decides a fault location and time, runs the workload to observe Symptoms, and either logs an unsuccessful attempt back into the loop or, once the oracle confirms reproduction, emits a reproduction script. Thick gray arrows carry one-shot inputs/outputs while thin blue arrows trace the iterative loop.
summary_zh: 图2示Anduril架构：Instrumenter静态分析系统代码，生成因果图与插桩系统；连同故障日志、oracle、workload输入Explorer，反馈循环中定位故障、运行、观察症状，成功输出复现脚本，否则记录重试。
notes: layout-proposal: pipeline-into-feedback-loop — a linear preprocessing pipeline (System code and other inputs into Instrumenter, then into Explorer) feeds an explicitly boxed cyclic sub-process (Update priorities to Fault location and time to Symptoms to Repro run logs and back to Explorer) that exits to a script once the oracle succeeds; none of the seven named templates captures this pipeline-feeding-a-labeled-cycle shape.
